title: EDGE: DBMS-Empowered Boolean Decomposition for GIG Synthesis
problem: Boolean decomposition-based logic synthesis is high-quality but computationally expensive, limiting application to large and complex logic functions in modern circuit design.
motivation: Decomposition-based synthesis yields superior results when combined with small-window optimization, but computational bottlenecks prevent scaling to industrial-scale gate-inverter graphs (GIGs).
method: Boolean decomposition breaks down logical functions (the mathematical rules that define how digital circuits behave) into simpler building blocks, but the traditional approach is slow because it tests candidate solutions one at a time. EDGE reformulates the problem as a database query: instead of iterating through possibilities sequentially, it asks the database to find all decompositions that satisfy certain criteria and evaluates them together. Database systems are highly optimized for exactly this kind of work—finding patterns in large sets of data and filtering efficiently—which makes generating and evaluating candidates for Gate-Inverter Graph synthesis (converting logic into circuits made of gates and inverters) much faster than the original method.
key_novelty: The key innovation is using database query optimization—techniques that efficiently handle large datasets—to speed up finding good Boolean decompositions for circuit synthesis.
contributions: Database-driven acceleration of Boolean decomposition achieving 21x runtime speedup
15% reduction in node count over state-of-the-art synthesis methods
DBMS framework enabling scalable decomposition for large/complex logic
limitations: Focus on GIG-based synthesis; applicability to other logic representations or synthesis flows not discussed.
primary_theme: Database acceleration for Boolean decomposition synthesis
